description.narrative: The Government of Botswana has since gazetted and enforced the EMERGENCY POWERS (COVID-19) REGULATIONS, 2020 that regulates the Declaration of lockdown, Work remotely from home and other Work arrangements in response to COVID-19. The Government of Botswana further adopted specific guidelines, such as Implementation of Return to work guidelines for COVID 19- dated 12 May 2020, Risk Mitigation Measures, dated 13th August 2020, and Circular on adoption of flexible working arrangements and related guidelines for decongestion in the world of work, dated 29th January 2021, to facilitate the operationalization of the Regulations. Since April 2020, Botswana benefited from ILO interventions aimed at assisting partners to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on workplaces and workers. The interventions include participation by 11 participants from Botswana in a series of OSH and COVID-19 trainings by ILO in collaboration with African Union Development Agency –New Partnership for Africa's Development (AUDA-NEPAD), guidance through and domestication of a series of Guidelines on COVID-19 and OSH by ILO in collaboration with AUDA-NEPAD into national guidelines and regulations on COVID-19, ILO's Webinar on COVID-19 for Labour and OSH Inspectorates in Southern African Development Community (SADC), ILO-supported series of trainings on OSH and Webinars via African Regional Labour Administration Centre (ARLAC), regular dissemination of new tools and up-to-date information, and financial support towards capacitation via ITCILO. The tripartite OSH taskforce received support to finalize the Terms of Reference for review of Factories Act into a gender-responsive and comprehensive OSH Act, and process for recruitment of the consultant has commenced. The ILO contributed technically into design of the training and guidelines' contents. The ILO also supported the organization of the webinar platform, enabling the virtual participation by member states.

Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
The Government of Botswana in close consultation with the Social Partners has instituted a process of labour law reform to strengthen social dialogue, collective bargaining, labour relations and improve working conditions in both the private sector and public service. To this end, Government reviewed and consolidated four pieces of legislation, namely, the Employment Act, the Trade Unions and Employers' Organizations Act, Trade Disputes Act, and the Public Service Act. Drafting instructions have been submitted to the Attorney General to formulate a consolidated bill on the revised legislation. It is envisaged that the bill will be presented in Parliament by end of September 2021 for enactment. The ILO provided technical support was provided to a Labour Law Review Committee to develop an Issues Paper to facilitate tripartite engagement on social dialogue to reach consensus on aspects of legislation requiring reform. ILO technical and advisory support was also provided in the drafting of terms of reference for the Labour Law Review Committee in order to facilitate its operations. Secondly, the ILO commissioned research in collaboration with SECTOR on comparative practices in collective bargaining, freedom of association and labour relations in the public service. Further research was commissioned in collaboration with the University of Cape Town on comparative practices on employment relationships and contracts of employment – focusing on flexible working hours, correctional service (freedom of association and CB for staff in Correctional Services).
The Office collaborated with the ITC-ILO to facilitate the participation of the tripartite partners represented in the Labour Law Committee to an e-Academy on Labour Law and Development in July 2021. The course sought to enhance the partners' capacity on key principles of labour law and its reform

description.narrative:
The Strategic Compliance Plan developed and adopted by the Labour Inspectorate of the Ministry of Labour (Date to be confirmed) and is being implemented in the Security sector. The compliance issues targeted by the Plan include Non-payment of wages, overtime, and compensation for injuries to address non-contribution by employers to the compensation fund.
Compliance measures in the Plan involve enforcement interventions relating to compliance issues identified (include Non-payment of wages, overtime, and compensation for injuries to address non-contribution by employers to the compensation fund). Secondly, since the bulk of security companies are contracted through Government tenders, systemic interventions by the labour inspectorate will involve collaborating with the Procurement of Asset and Disposal Board to ensure that Government tenders factor in compliance with labour legislation. Thirdly, to foster cooperation between the labour inspectorate with the Ministry of Defence which registers security companies and has the mandate to inspect compliance by security companies in accordance with legislation. Finally, education and awareness raising campaign for both employers and workers in the security sector on provisions of the legislation on the compliance issues identified above.
A total of 204 enterprises have been identified to-date within the Security sector to pilot the Strategic Compliance Plan.
The strategic compliance plan in Botswana is well underway with 55% (16 out of 29) of Strategic Compliance actions devised in the plan completed. This includes 58% of the enforcement intervention, 50% of the communication and 57% of the systemic interventions completed. The ILO collaborated with LABADMIN-OSH to facilitate a Strategic Compliance Planning workshop (JANUARY 2021). Some of the key objectives of the training workshop were to introduce the Strategic Compliance Planning methodology to achieve compliance outcomes, to provide guidance on how to develop a Strategic Compliance Plan based on available resources and on how to pilot it in selected priority sectors. Additional objectives of the training were to build capacity of the inspectors on the use of the Strategic Compliance Planning Portal, and to assist the inspectors to develop a short term inspection strategy for a discreet compliance issue.
Focusing on the security sectors, a draft Strategic Compliance Plan was developed at the training workshop and later refined for adoption in February 2021 by the Ministry of Labour. The Strategic Compliance Plan includes a focus on enforcement, education and awareness raising, and systemic interventions. ILO advisory support was also provided towards the implementation of the strategic compliance plan. The ILO made inputs into the awareness raising messages in brochures developed to sensitize employers and workers on provisions of the law in the identified sector. Brochures developed are aimed at educating workers of their rights in the sectors and obligations of employers.
